citation.title: Modeling Missing Data in Clinical Time Series with RNNs
citation.authors: Zachary C. Lipton; David C. Kale; Randall Wetzel
citation.venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning for Healthcare 2016 (JMLR W&C Track)

topic: Missing-data indicators and imputation for RNN, MLP and logistic-regression multilabel classification of irregularly sampled clinical time series.
own_question: Can binary missingness indicators and hand-engineered missingness features improve diagnosis classification from discretized PICU sequences, compared with zero-filling and forward-fill imputation?
actual_method_and_evidence: The authors used about 10,401 CHLA PICU episodes with 13 hourly-binned variables and 128 diagnosis labels. They compared zero-fill, forward-fill/median imputation, indicators, and combinations across LSTM, MLP and logistic regression on one 80/10/10 split. The best reported micro AUC was 0.8730 for an LSTM using zeros plus indicators. Labels are static diagnoses; this is not nowcasting.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: In one clinical time-series study, irregular sampling discretized onto fixed time steps created missingness patterns. Adding binary missingness indicators to recurrent models improved reported classification over imputation alone.
claim_checks.qualification: Applies to a single dataset and split, with medical labels and a non-causal classification target. It offers at most an analogy for representing CES-report staleness or absence as an input; this paper did not test that use.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Hourly bins with forward-fill; inference uses the final step for a static label. No report latency or arrival timing is modeled.
validation_if_relevant: Single train/validation/test split; no external or untouched data.
forbidden_inferences: Missingness indicators will improve BES/ECEI CES nowcasting
Evidence about plasma diagnostics or causal estimators
Applicability of zero-fill findings to our inputs
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include optionally as a cross-domain example motivating explicit encoding of report staleness or availability. It is not plasma evidence and has no bearing on the novelty or performance framing.
